thread:
Maya K: Reviewing an alternate Compact list idea for Routing policies. Main changes: priority pills instead of numeric column, inline validation badges, and a small per-row Preview toggle that expands a micro-sim. Link: https://www.figma.com/file/efgh5678/compact-priority-pills

Maya K: Questions I want input on:
  • priority pill contrast + semantics (is color + label enough?)
  • whether Preview should animate open inline or open a flyout (perf vs context)
  • suggested copy for the validation badge when a rule is shadowed
  • how to signal reordering state to screen readers in a dense list

Ravi P: Quick first pass:
  - Pill idea is nice for density. But color must meet 4.5:1 for normal text if we rely on color to indicate priority. Consider adding a small chevron icon inside the pill for non-color cues.
  - Inline micro-sim sounds useful, but if it runs a call we should debounce it and show a skeleton; otherwise the list janks.

Chen L: Accessibility notes:
  - Use aria-roledescription="draggable list" on the list container.
  - For lift/drop: Space to pick up, Arrow Up/Down to move, Space to drop; announce with aria-live: "Moved to position 2 of 8".
  - If we use pills, ensure the pill text is real text (not background image) so magnifiers can read it.

Nina V: Copy proposals for shadowing/shunting:
  - Short badge (in red outline): "Overridden" with tooltip: "This rule never matches because a higher-priority rule handles these predicates. See conflict." 
  - Tooltip body should include a quick link: "View conflicting rule" which opens the conflicting rule in a side panel.

Design Bot: Design token warnings from preview branch:
  - warn: token color-priority-1-500 fails contrast at 14px
  - note: compact-row-height variable clashes with workspace token set

Maya K: On animation: Chen, you mentioned skeletons/debounce. If Preview is inline and animated, we should use transform/opacity only and avoid layout thrash. If heavy, open a flyout anchored to the row.

Ravi P: Suggestion: default to inline collapsed micro-sim (show counts + matched example) that is purely client-side using cached samples. Only run the full server sim on explicit "Run preview" in the flyout. That reduces accidental expensive sims.

Chen L: Good call. Also, for screen readers: when the inline micro-sim expands, set focus to the micro-sim heading and provide a "Close preview" button. Avoid surprising focus jumps.

Nina V: Microcopy: when a rule is "Overridden" the tooltip line can say: "Rule overridden by Rule #" — but we prefer not to surface raw IDs. Use description: "overridden by \"Block internal traffic\"".

Maya K: UX polish idea: when reordering, transiently show an inline label near the handle: "Dropping in position 4" so keyboard users get visual feedback too.

Ravi P: Implementation note: backend will accept reorder events as minimal payload. If we do optimistic UI we need clear rollback behaviour and a queued save indicator per-row.

Design Bot: Also flagged an eslint console.warn in reorder-button in the branch: https://preview.redwood.test/branches/compact-pills build 2025-10-02_09:05

Chen L: Test cases to add:
  - SR announces position and previews open/close
  - color contrast for priority pills at common text sizes
  - optimistic reorder + failed save rollback
  - tooltip link opens conflicting rule side panel

Maya K: Action items:
  - @Nina V finalize badge + tooltip copy and paste strings here
  - @Ravi P draft the client-side micro-sim fallback + flyout flow
  - @Chen L add aria examples to Figma and a short SR script
  - @DevOps (hand off) address the eslint warn and token clash

Nina V: I'll drop the copy in 30m. Example badge strings: ["Overridden", "Matches fewer inputs", "No matches in sample"]. Tooltip long form ready shortly.

Maya K: Nice. Let's target merging the design + accessibility notes this sprint and keep Preview default to collapsed to avoid perf surprises. Thanks! :sparkles:
